steps.what: 19. Heal guard: IsEnding && !IsPlayer -> return. There is NO dead guard
steps.issue: CORRECTED 2026-08-01 (round 13, R11). The equivalence this closure rests on is FALSE, not imprecise: `combat.is_over` is `phase == Phase.COMBAT_OVER`, which mirrors C#'s `!IsInProgress`, NOT `IsEnding`. CombatManager.IsEnding (CombatManager.cs:180-202) OPENS with `if (!IsInProgress) return false;`, so it is true exactly DURING the ending sequence and false again the instant combat is torn down -- the COMPLEMENTARY window to the sim's guard. CreatureCmd.Heal (CreatureCmd.cs:691-696) gates on the bare IsEnding. EXECUTED WITNESS, BOTH DIRECTIONS: with every enemy dead but combat not torn down (phase PLAYER_TURN, is_over False, is_ending True) `CreatureCmd.heal(enemy, 7)` returns 7 where C# REFUSES; with phase COMBAT_OVER (is_over True, is_ending False) it returns 0 where C# PERMITS. So a non-player heal reached in the window between the killing blow and teardown -- an on-death effect healing a surviving ally, Illusion's REVIVE, Adaptable's respawn, Reattach -- is wrongly ALLOWED by the sim. The correct predicate here is `combat.is_ending`, and specifically NOT `combat.is_over_or_ending`, which would OVER-GUARD the post-teardown heal C# permits. ADJACENT TO, NOT IDENTICAL WITH, seam/hook_dispatch's F3: F3's site is HookSystem.combat_is_over, read by _each for the 73 gated dispatch names, whose C# counterpart is IterateCombatHookListeners' IsOverOrEnding (Hook.cs:53-63). CreatureCmd.heal is not a hook dispatch, is not in _COMBAT_GATED_HOOKS, and never reaches that gate -- it reads combat.is_over directly. Same root confusion, two different sites, TWO DIFFERENT CORRECT REPLACEMENTS; one fix cannot close both.  The text it replaced read: Closed 2026-07-27: CreatureCmd.heal's `if target.is_dead: return 0` is gone. The only early return left is `combat.is_over and target.side != 'player'` (sts2_rl/cmds.py), which is CreatureCmd.cs:693-696's `IsEnding && !IsPlayer` and nothing more. The docstring records why the change was forced: with a prevented death now left at 0 HP, the old guard would have blocked the very revives it existed for.

guards.what: G4 (dormant) -- CreatureCmd.heal refuses to heal a dead creature; C#'s Heal revives
guards.issue: CORRECTED 2026-08-01 (round 13, R11). The equivalence this closure rests on is FALSE, not imprecise: `combat.is_over` is `phase == Phase.COMBAT_OVER`, which mirrors C#'s `!IsInProgress`, NOT `IsEnding`. CombatManager.IsEnding (CombatManager.cs:180-202) OPENS with `if (!IsInProgress) return false;`, so it is true exactly DURING the ending sequence and false again the instant combat is torn down -- the COMPLEMENTARY window to the sim's guard. CreatureCmd.Heal (CreatureCmd.cs:691-696) gates on the bare IsEnding. EXECUTED WITNESS, BOTH DIRECTIONS: with every enemy dead but combat not torn down (phase PLAYER_TURN, is_over False, is_ending True) `CreatureCmd.heal(enemy, 7)` returns 7 where C# REFUSES; with phase COMBAT_OVER (is_over True, is_ending False) it returns 0 where C# PERMITS. So a non-player heal reached in the window between the killing blow and teardown -- an on-death effect healing a surviving ally, Illusion's REVIVE, Adaptable's respawn, Reattach -- is wrongly ALLOWED by the sim. The correct predicate here is `combat.is_ending`, and specifically NOT `combat.is_over_or_ending`, which would OVER-GUARD the post-teardown heal C# permits. ADJACENT TO, NOT IDENTICAL WITH, seam/hook_dispatch's F3: F3's site is HookSystem.combat_is_over, read by _each for the 73 gated dispatch names, whose C# counterpart is IterateCombatHookListeners' IsOverOrEnding (Hook.cs:53-63). CreatureCmd.heal is not a hook dispatch, is not in _COMBAT_GATED_HOOKS, and never reaches that gate -- it reads combat.is_over directly. Same root confusion, two different sites, TWO DIFFERENT CORRECT REPLACEMENTS; one fix cannot close both. guards.issue: C# carries TWO INTEGERS on CardSelectorPrefs (:25-27) that every consumer derives from: the confirm button (NDeckEnchantSelectScreen:176, `MinSelect != MaxSelect && selected >= MinSelect`), the completion bounds check (:270), and the automated selector call `Selector.GetSelectedCards(list, MinSelect, MaxSelect)` (CardSelectCmd.cs:582). The sim re-encodes this as `driver.SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES`, a frozenset of purpose STRINGS living in a DIFFERENT FILE from the call site that has the numbers; `RunDriver._card_selector` derives exactly ONE boolean from it, and that boolean is the ENTIRE surface through which a driver-attached policy can decline a pick. The `min_select` a call site passes only reaches the SELECTORLESS fallback -- a path no production driver takes. STRUCTURALLY LOSSY, three ways: (1) it can only express `MinSelect in {0, count}`, never a genuine 1..N-1 floor; (2) it forces a PURPOSE FORK whenever a MinSelect-0 screen shares a verb with an exact-count screen -- five forks exist already (transform/transform_optional, choose_a_card/_optional, exhaust/exhaust_any, discard/discard_any, enchant/enchant_optional) and a sixth is owed for `from_discard`; (3) THE TWO HALVES CAN SILENTLY DISAGREE, and they do at THREE LIVE SITES TODAY -- potions.py:1012 (Ashwater), potions.py:273 (Gambler's Brew), cards/neows_fury.py:73. All three pass min_select=0 and are force-filled anyway through the real production driver (EXECUTED: Ashwater's 5-card hand goes to 0 with ZERO decisions raised). A call site that correctly passes the number LOOKS right on an isolated read. The faithful port is min/max on the prefs, derived at the call site.
